catalog_quote: Tal is a tone language, like all Nigerian languages, with the exception of Fulani (Williamson 1984). The language contrasts three level tones, namely H(igh), M(id) and L(ow). In addition to the level tones, the language also contrasts the contour tone HR, which is a raised H tone. As shown in (5), the tones mark both lexical and grammatical distinctions. ... [p. 8] The data in (6) shows that all the combinatorial possibilities are attested for the cooccurrence of level tones, but we find no instances where the HR tone occurs as the final tone of a monomorphemic word with two or more syllables. ... Considering that a bimoraic syllable in Tal can have two tones and in line with the proposal in Yip (2002), we assume that the TBU in Tal is a mora. Throughout this work, tones of all Tal examples are fully marked.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Tal (Mudak variety) is described as a lexical/grammatical tone language with three level tones (H, M, L) plus a raised-high contour (HR) restricted to word-initial position; the mora is the tone-bearing unit. The source makes no claim about word stress or accent; the only prominence remark is that the word-initial TBU is 'perceptually prominent' (licenses the contour tone, keeps its lexical tone under deictic tonal overwriting), which is a positional-faithfulness argument rather than a stress rule.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Tonal: HR never occurs as the final tone of a polysyllabic monomorphemic word; all level-tone combinations attested.
new_statements.domain_note: Statements concern lexical tone on words in isolation (F0 plots from monomoraic words spoken and hummed in isolation by the native-speaker co-author) and grammatical tone in N+modifier phrases; no word-stress domain discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: Akinbo & Bulkaam 2024 describe the Muɗak variety of Tal (one of six varieties: Muɗak, Mbaal, Mungƙoot, Muɗong, Bongmut, Takong; differences said to be only segmental/tonal in some words). Glottolog tall1250 has no dialect subcodes; Blench groups Tal with Koenoem and Pyapung as 'Talic' within West Chadic A3.

sources.note: Sec. 2 (Mudak variety) gives consonants, vowels, moraic syllable, and 2.2 Tone (p.6): 'Tal is a tone language.. three level tones H, M, L + contour HR'; TBU = mora; all Tal data fully tone-marked. No statement about word stress or accent anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent = 0). Secs. 4.2/5 call the word-initial TBU the 'perceptually prominent position' (contour tone restricted to word-initial position) in a positional-faithfulness argument, not a stress claim.
